seo_title: Cost of Living in Budapest 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Budapest per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A European capital on the Danube with history and prices that are affordable by EU standards. Schengen access, clear healthcare and education, but a difficult language and slow bureaucracy.
pros: Schengen visa — free movement across the EU
Affordable rent for a European capital
Developed healthcare and education (including tuition-free universities)
An active IT scene and startup community
A warm continental climate — summers up to +30°C
cons: Hungarian is one of the hardest languages in Europe
Strict visa and banking requirements for Russians

faq.question: Do I need to learn Hungarian in Budapest?
faq.answer: Not for daily life — English is enough in Budapest. For paperwork and long-term integration, yes.

faq.question: What about visas for Russians in Budapest?
faq.answer: Tourist Schengen visas aren't issued. Only a long-stay D visa through work, study or family.

faq.question: How long does a residence permit take in Budapest?
faq.answer: From application to decision: 30–90 days. Bureaucracy is slow and requires patience.

faq.question: Where to live in Budapest?
faq.answer: Districts VI and VII are the trendy centre. XIII is business-oriented, IX is creative. Further out it's calmer and cheaper.

faq.question: What are IT salaries in Budapest?
faq.answer: Middle €2,500–4,000 net, Senior €4,000–6,500. Taxes are around 33%.

faq.question: Can I get permanent residency in Budapest?
faq.answer: After 3 years of legal residence; citizenship after 8 years.

reviews.text: Budapest offers European life at an affordable price. The downside — without Hungarian, paperwork takes a while and banks are cautious.
Architecture, thermal baths, walks along the Danube. But Schengen was hard for me — I had to legalise through study.
